newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end higher, off sharp early gains.
newsitem.headline: India shares end higher, off sharp early gains.

text.p: A three-day old market rally showed signs of faltering by close of trade on Wednesday, as a bout of profit-taking by speculators wiped out sharp early gains, dealers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index jumped 67.70 points, or 2.3 percent, to an intra-day high of 3,051.72 before dropping to end at 3,001.24.
"The market's taken a breather... the brake has been put on the sharp spurt in prices," said a dealer at a local firm.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 9.66 points, or 1.13 percent, to close at 860.40.

Analysts see the depressed market bottoming out after discounting a series of negative factors, such as an economic slowdown, poor first-half company results and the coalition government's inability to push through liberalisation measures.
"The selling frenzy in the recent past was the result of all-round pessimism ...with valuations counting for little," said Ramnath Iyer, strategist at Peregrine Capital.
Bombay stocks which fell to a three-year low of 2,713.12 on December 4, have gained about 10.5 percent from that level.
The markets have surged about 4 percent this week.
Some dealers said news that former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao had been asked to quit as chief of the Congress Parliamentary Party might help improve sentiment.
Local funds were buyers in front-bencher stocks, they said.
ACC rose 13.50 rupees to 1,129.50, Glaxo 11.20 to 247.0 Bajaj Auto 4.75 to 797.25, and Tata Chemicals 4.50 to 168.0.
Reliance and SBI were unchanged at 194.25 and 218.50 rupees.
"In short term the market was in an over-bought condition. I feel that it should witness some correction before staging another rally," said Ajit Sial of Delhi brokers Sial and Co.
